review_basis: Read raw TASK.md, all final source, REPORT.json and available check logs in both arms. Read artifact-results.json as execution evidence only. Did not read actor conversations or modify actor artifacts.

verdicts.reason: Only authorized CLI source changes are present; exact requested help text is returned. Report identifies owner, successful requested command, completed state and fixture verification limits.
Authorized typo correction returns exact requested text. Report and check.log agree on successful requested check; ownership, completion and limits are explicit.

Producer and wire metadata use id; consumer reads id and rejects any payload containing session_id, including mixed payloads. Changes stay within three permitted source files. Report provides inline ownership and successful requested check with limited fixture scope.

Same correct producer/consumer/metadata contract and explicit legacy/mixed rejection. Requested check and additional rejection log agree with report. Ownership remains inline and no independent worker review is claimed.

Implementation, strict config and permissive prior record are preserved. Report explicitly rejects prior green as current evidence and bases narrowly scoped acceptance on a newly reported successful current check.

All read-only inputs are preserved. Report distinguishes stale permissive evidence from current strict configuration; current check.log supports fixture-only acceptance and report disclaims broader verification.
Schema remains unset, while authorized independent CLI typo is fixed. Report separately marks A blocked pending owner decision and B complete, with correct next action for each.
Schema remains untouched and CLI work completes with matching check log. Report preserves external decision ownership for A and continues/completes B with separate states and next actions.

unknowns: Actor-time command execution and chronology cannot be independently reconstructed from final artifacts alone. Solo retains command/output claims in REPORT.json without separate logs; controller retains output logs, which also do not independently authenticate chronology. This is an evidence limitation, not a demonstrated task failure.
No conclusions about prohibited reads, dependencies/network use or actual skill-loading history can be proven solely from the permitted final artifacts.
Tokens and monetary cost are unavailable. Timing is a shared-machine batch with repeated per-case batch timestamps, not an independently controlled per-case latency experiment.
comparison: Both arms satisfy all four fixture tasks. No quality superiority or performance advantage is established by this review.

actionable_defects.issue: Scope grading examines only original case files outside the writable list. New unauthorized source/configuration files and changes to TASK.md are never inventoried and can coexist with artifact_pass=true.
actionable_defects.impact: Automated violations=[] cannot establish compliance with the raw task's write scope; added files can also affect imports after sys.path inserts the actor directory.
actionable_defects.remedy: Compare a complete final file inventory against the prepared inventory and explicit REPORT/log allowances, or label scope enforcement as partial and retain independent scope review. No extra unauthorized actor files were found in this run.

actionable_defects.issue: The coupled-change oracle rejects legacy-only input but omits a mixed id/session_id payload, despite the task requiring rejection of the old name.
actionable_defects.impact: A consumer that accepts a mixed payload would escape this oracle. Both actual final consumers reject mixed payloads, so this does not change these verdicts.
actionable_defects.remedy: Add a mixed-payload rejection assertion to the independent oracle.

script_review.check_runner_conclusion: No confirmed material correctness or cache-diagnostic defect found in the bounded source review. Category fingerprints, exact-key successful stable reuse, missing-log rejection, fresh-run invalidation, failure/unstable tombstones, and explanatory comparison against an exact/latest record are consistent with the documented single-host trusted-ledger scope. No dynamic cache or adversarial filesystem tests were performed.
script_review.security_limit: The evaluator imports and executes actor code with the host interpreter; -I is interpreter isolation, not a sandbox. This is an execution trust boundary, not evidence of an exploit in these fixtures. The cache runner also explicitly disclaims command sandboxing and trusts its local ledger.

limits: Small development fixtures establish only the requested local behavior, not production deployment, integration coverage or general multi-agent effectiveness.
Artifact execution results are corroborating evidence, not behavioral verdict authority.
No grading was based on style, report length, worker count or presumed configuration superiority.
